prompt: Write three varargs formatting helpers that all have to behave sensibly when zero arguments are passed. Complete joinNonNull, bulletList, and describe, then run the tests.
explanation: Inside the method a varargs parameter is simply an array, so parts.length and a for-each loop are all you need -- and an empty call site gives you a zero-length array rather than null. Appending the separator only when the builder is not yet empty is what keeps it strictly BETWEEN items, which also handles leading nulls correctly. describe shows why varargs and arrays are interchangeable: passing new int[] {4, 9} works exactly like passing 4, 9.
hints: A varargs parameter is an array inside the method: loop over parts with a for-each and use items.length for the count.
To put the separator only between kept values, append it before the next value whenever the StringBuilder is already non-empty -- that way nulls you skipped leave no stray separators.
describe needs three cases: zero values, exactly one ("value"), and more ("values"); java.util.Arrays.toString(values) already formats as [1, 2, 3].
